text:
Connor O'Brien: Go/no-go for enabling *profile pack defaults* in Hosted as part of runtime-1.22. Target: flip flag for small canary cohort today if we have sign-off from Runtime + SRE + Infra. Checklist here (WIP): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENG/runtime-1-22-profile-pack-launch

Talia Benson: Adding context: scope is Hosted-only defaulting to profile-pack v1.0 for H100 + L40S pools. Dedicated remains opt-in (pin supported). Private unaffected unless they set Helm values. We need to confirm rollback semantics + dashboards.

Mateo Alvarez: Runtime side: code paths are in behind flag. PRs landed: loader+schema validation, selection logic, scheduler buckets, kernel v3 for H100, KV compaction counters, observability tags. Biggest risk is tail latency under mixed prompt shapes if batching gets too aggressive (we already backed off once).

Sean Gallagher: SRE gating items I need before I say yes:
1) Kill switch is *one knob* that reverts to previous defaults (not just “don’t select new profile”).
2) Dashboards show p50/p95/p99 by `profile_id` + `sku`, plus queueing (`scheduler_queue_ms`).
3) Rollback playbook link + who is on point.

Allison Grant: Dashboards are ready in staging + prod (hidden) via observability-pack/pr-221. Panels:
- Profile adoption
- p95/p99 latency by profile
- kernel fallback rate
- KV compaction time + fragmentation estimate
- scheduler_queue_ms
If folks want, I can unhide prod dashboard after this thread.

Neha Kapoor: Infra notes: fleet heterogeneity is mostly driver version variance. H100 pools are consistent enough, L40S is more mixed. We need to be explicit that selection includes driver/CUDA gate and that mismatches do NOT silently pick a weird profile.

Irene Choi: +1. For L40S especially, we’ve seen nodes lagging a minor driver patch. If the selection logic falls back to “closest match”, I’m nervous.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel side: H100 attention kernel v3 is default *only* when we detect supported driver range. Otherwise we stay on v2. We also export `kernel_choice` and `kernel_fallback_total` counters now.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduler buckets are now: short/medium/long prefill and decode. Default queue policy tries to protect decode tail latency when long-prefill requests show up. We should keep canary traffic mixed (don’t pick only the easy cohort).

Rafael Mendes: Rollback: for Hosted, we can flip flag off globally (config push) which reverts to old heuristic defaults. There’s also a “force profile_version=disabled” override on the control plane side. Both are audited. I’ll paste exact steps once Sean confirms which one he wants as primary.

Sean Gallagher: Primary should be global kill switch (flag off) + verify effect within 5 min. Secondary is profile_version pin if we need to isolate a region/cohort. Also need on-call comms template for incident channel.

Omar El-Sayed: On the “one knob” point: flag off disables profile selection and ignores profile config entirely; runtime goes back to legacy knobs. That’s implemented in pr-24979 + pr-25049 startup log summary prints `profile_mode=disabled` when off.

Connor O'Brien: Can someone link the flag name + current default value in prod?

Omar El-Sayed: Flag is `runtime.profile_pack.enabled` (bool). In prod now: false. Canary target would be 1% traffic in `us-west2` + `us-east1` for H100 pools only.

Neha Kapoor: If we do L40S today, I want concurrency caps in place. We’ve had intermittent OOM under burst traffic.

Mateo Alvarez: L40S got a safer default cap + more headroom in pr-24918 and follow-up tuning pr-25071. But I agree: don’t expand to L40S until we see stable H100 canary.

Lauren Bishop: From Dedicated/Product: please keep Dedicated opt-in for at least a week after Hosted canary starts. We already have customer comms drafted around “pin/rollback”, but we should avoid surprise perf changes in contract SLO contexts.

Talia Benson: Proposal to de-risk: Phase 1 today = H100 Hosted canary only (1%). Phase 2 (48h later) = expand canary to 5% + include L40S if dashboards look clean.

Allison Grant: Works for me. Dashboard can filter by sku=H100 and profile_id. If we don’t enable L40S, I’ll still keep panels ready.

Irene Choi: Infra sign-off for Phase 1 (H100 only) provided:
- no silent “closest match” profile selection for mismatched drivers
- explicit log + metric on compatibility rejection

Omar El-Sayed: Compatibility behavior: if driver/CUDA outside supported range, we *reject* profile and fall back to legacy defaults, and emit `profile_compat_reject_total{reason=...}`. Also logs “profile_compat=reject” with detected versions.

Sean Gallagher: Good. For SRE sign-off, I want the alert thresholds called out:
- p99 latency regression gate (vs baseline)
- error rate gate
- kernel fallback spike gate
- OOM / CUDA error spike gate

Allison Grant: Alerting is partially wired. Current proposed thresholds (for canary only):
- p99 latency +15% for 10m triggers page
- 5xx +0.3% absolute for 10m triggers page
- kernel_fallback_rate > 2% for 15m triggers ticket (page if > 5%)
- cuda_oom_total > 0 sustained triggers page
These are in the dashboard spec doc; can be adjusted.

Mateo Alvarez: Runtime sign-off for Phase 1. Caveat: if we see scheduler_queue_ms increase without GPU util increase, that’s a bad sign (queue policy issue). We should watch that closely.

Sofia Ivanova: Agree; and if we see p99 spikes correlated with long-prefill bucket saturation, we should either tighten admission control or reduce max batch for that bucket.

Rafael Mendes: Rollback steps (Hosted):
1) Flip `runtime.profile_pack.enabled=false` via fleet config push (takes ~2-3 min to propagate).
2) Confirm in `/health` debug fields show `profile_pack_enabled=false` and legacy knobs active (sampled on 3 pods/region).
3) Verify adoption panel goes to ~0 within 10 min.
4) Post update in #incidents if paging, otherwise #eng-runtime.
Owner on point: me + Sean.

Connor O'Brien: Any remaining blockers before I ask deploy to proceed?

Neha Kapoor: Infra ok with H100-only canary. Please exclude any pools with known driver variance (I can DM list). Also: make sure B200 detection doesn’t accidentally start selecting anything in Hosted (we have a couple early nodes in lab, but shouldn’t be in prod).

Omar El-Sayed: B200 is hard-gated in pr-24927: runtime refuses to enable profile pack on B200 unless an explicit profile_version is set (and it logs loudly). Shouldn’t affect Hosted prod.

Sean Gallagher: SRE sign-off for Phase 1, assuming canary cohort is truly 1% and we have a human watching dashboards for first hour.

Talia Benson: I’ll be watcher for first hour (and Mateo as backup). I’ll start a quick notes doc for observations.

DeployBot: :rocket: Deploy started: runtime-1.22.0 to Hosted canary cohort (1% H100) (requested by Connor O'Brien). Tracking: https://deploy.redwoodinference.com/runs/hosted/77219

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: Thanks. Please drop here when canary is live and dashboards confirm profile adoption.

Allison Grant: Canary looks live. Adoption panel: ~0.9% of H100 traffic on `profile_pack_v1.0` (profile_id `h100_default_v1`). No L40S adoption.

Sean Gallagher: Watching p99 + error rate. First 10m looks flat. Kernel fallback rate ~0.3% (expected).

Mateo Alvarez: Confirmed startup logs in canary pods show detected sku=H100, driver in supported range, kernel_choice=h100_attn_v3. No compat rejects so far.

Connor O'Brien: OK, calling Phase 1 a go. Keep canary at 1% until tomorrow morning unless we see a regression. Please log any anomalies + links here so we can include in release notes.

Talia Benson: Noted. Next check-in: 09:00 PT tomorrow for Phase 2 decision (expand cohort + consider L40S).
